title: Who Really Holds Your Crypto? Exchange vs Your Own Wallet
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. Crypto on an exchange is held by the exchange; in a self-custody wallet you hold the keys. Each has trade-offs. Sources: Investopedia, Coinbase Learn. AI-generated voice. Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: WHO HOLDS IT?
scenes.narration: You bought crypto. But who actually holds it? The answer depends on where you keep it.

scenes.head: ON AN EXCHANGE
scenes.narration: On an exchange, the company holds the keys for you. It is easy to use, but you trust the company.

scenes.head: SELF-CUSTODY
scenes.narration: In self-custody, you hold the keys yourself. You get full control, and full responsibility too.

scenes.head: THE CATCH
scenes.sub: LOST KEYS CAN MEAN LOST COINS
scenes.narration: The catch is that nobody can reset a lost recovery phrase. If it is gone, the coins can be gone.

scenes.head: THE OTHER RISK
scenes.narration: Exchanges carry their own risk, like hacks or frozen withdrawals. It is a trade-off between convenience and control.

scenes.head: BASIC HABITS
scenes.narration: Either way, use two-factor login, never share your recovery phrase, and test with small amounts first.
